In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative oxygen consumption of the various components of brain is: (a) axoplasmic components, 30 per cent; (b) non-neuronal cellular elements, 60 per cent; (c) neurones, 10 per cent.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the glial cells are capable of a respiratory activity comparable to that of the neurones, that the axoplasm of white matter has a respiratory rate equivalent to about one-half that of neurones and that the respiratory activity of glial cells is not necessarily dependent upon the presence of neurones.
the glial cells in the cerebral cortex of the rabbit have an oxygen consumption rate equivalent to 4-6 X pl/hr per glial cell.
the oxygen consumption of cerebral white matter is accounted for by the sum of the respiratory activity of axons and cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the oxygen consumption of glial cells is much greater than that of neurons.
glial cells are responsible for a significant portion of the oxygen consumed by the brain.
the relative respiration rate of the various structural components of the nervous system is of importance in considering the metabolic role of the various constituents.
